outcome: No resolution of the classical statement since 26 January 2024. Two new partial results: Chen et al. (arXiv:2602.05090, Feb 2026, produced by AxiomProver) show that for almost all primes the even eigenspaces A_p(ω^{2k}) vanish for an initial range of indices 2 ≤ 2k ≤ √p/(log p)^α; Guo–Tao (arXiv:2609.13932, Sep 2026) show A_34 = 0 for every odd prime and density-one vanishing in certain residue classes for d in {4,6}. Qin (Acta Math. Sinica 2024) claims A_0, A_2, …, A_32 vanish, with scope over primes unstated in the abstract. A full claimed proof by Stolin (arXiv:2001.09702, 2020) predates the window, has no publication or published review, and is treated here as unverified.
problem_asks: One universal claim, with no separable parts. For every prime p, p does not divide h⁺(p), the class number of the maximal real subfield Q(ζ_p)⁺ of the p-th cyclotomic field. The quantifier runs over all primes (no bound), and the condition is p ∤ h⁺(p) at each. The standard equivalent for odd p: the plus part of the p-part of the class group of Q(ζ_p) is trivial, i.e. A_p(ω^{2k}) = 0 for every even 2k with 2 ≤ 2k ≤ p−3 (ω the Teichmüller character), so every even eigenspace must vanish. The statement names no other quantity and does not restrict to regular or irregular primes, degree, or eigenspace index.

events.what_happened: Buhler and Harvey, 'Irregular primes to 163 million' (arXiv:0912.2121). Computes all irregular primes below 163,577,356 and verifies the Kummer–Vandiver conjecture for each of them, and that the λ-invariant equals the index of irregularity. Published in Mathematics of Computation in 2011 per a search listing (AMS page not opened).
events.delivers: Finite verification: for every odd prime p below 163,577,356, p does not divide h⁺(p). This is a check of finitely many instances of the universal claim, not a restriction of it.
events.remains: Every prime p ≥ 163,577,356, i.e. the universal claim as stated.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published 2011 per a search listing; the referee process was not seen

events.directly_checkable: Computation only (irregular indices and λ-invariants of each prime below the bound). Not checkable by hand for a single object.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture at every checked prime; no counterexample below the bound.

events.what_happened: Mihăilescu, 'Turning Washington's heuristics in favor of Vandiver's conjecture' (arXiv:1011.6283). Conditional on Greenberg's conjecture for the p-th cyclotomic extensions, shows that if Vandiver's conjecture fails at p then the λ⁻ defect is correlated with the irregularity index, and argues this favours Vandiver. Not an unconditional result. No journal reference found.
events.revisions: v1 29 Nov 2010; v2 29 Oct 2012 (adds three variants of the proof 'in sequel to an interesting discussion with a colleague').
events.delivers: A conditional consequence (of Greenberg's conjecture and of failure of the conjecture at p). Does not prove or disprove the conjecture at any prime.
events.time_since_posted: about 16 years; no journal publication or citing work found
events.direction: Heuristic argument in favour of the conjecture, conditional on assumptions the abstract states; makes no unconditional claim.

events.what_happened: Stolin, 'Vandiver's Conjecture via K-theory' (arXiv:2001.09702). Abstract: 'The aim of this paper is to prove Vandiver's conjecture, which has several consequences including the first case of Fermat's Great Theorem.' The main text (ar5iv rendering of v4) reaches 'Section 3, Theorem 3.6: r₊ = 0' and closes with 'The theorem and Vandiver's conjecture are proved.' Method: a Mayer–Vietoris sequence, the Kervaire–Murthy computation, and structure results from Stolin (1994) on Pic(ℤC_{p²}). Preprint only; no journal reference, and the arXiv page shows no withdrawal. The author is listed as Professor Emeritus, Chalmers (Chalmers seminar page).
events.revisions: v1 27 Jan 2020; v2 3 Mar 2020; v3 12 Mar 2020; v4 15 Jun 2020 (latest listed). The v4 main text says: 'As a result of that questions, in the main text of the paper I replaced the proof of of Theorem 3.6 with a new one.'
events.delivers: If the argument is correct, the full classical statement: for every odd prime p, the even part of the class group is trivial (r₊ = 0), i.e. p ∤ h⁺(p) for all p. The paper claims the whole problem, not a restricted case.
events.remains: Nothing, if the argument holds. Several steps are sketched or cited rather than proved (see doubts).
events.time_since_posted: 6 years 8 months; no journal, published review, refutation or citing work found in searches
events.directly_checkable: The argument is algebra in the paper's text (Theorem 3.6 and the appendix). No object to check by hand.
events.doubts: (1) The v4 text says the author 'replaced the proof of Theorem 3.6' in the main text after questions from readers. (2) The extension of an earlier computation from primes satisfying Vandiver's conjecture to all primes is sketched: 'computed in [2] for the primes satisfying Vandiver's conjecture. However, similar computations can be done for any prime' (§1.1). (3) 'Then clearly q=1' follows a limiting argument that is only sketched (§3, Theorem 3.6). (4) Load-bearing inputs are cited, not proved: Stolin (1994) Lemma 2 and a mod-p norm fact (§1.2, §2 Claim 2), a norm-residue identity from Cassels–Fröhlich (§2 Claim 1), and Kummer's lemma with no citation (§1.4). (5) Leopoldt's conjecture for the relevant field is used and described as known, without citation (§3). Separately, the author's Chalmers seminar abstract (10 Mar 2023) describes the approach as 'to prove the Kummer-Vandiver conjecture using a fine structure of the Picard group'; it carries the parenthetical '(this statemnt needs to be confirmed)' about a historical attribution (Vandiver implying the first case of Fermat), not about the proof. These are the points a checker would need to resolve; none is a verdict.
events.direction: Claims to prove the conjecture for all odd primes, i.e. in the direction the problem asserts.

events.what_happened: Hart, Harvey and Ong, 'Irregular primes to two billion' (arXiv:1605.02398). Computes all irregular primes below 2^31 = 2,147,483,648 and 'verify[s] the Kummer-Vandiver conjecture for each of these primes'. Published in Mathematics of Computation, vol. 86 (2017), pp. 3031–3049, per a search listing (AMS page not opened). Wikipedia's article gives the bound as '231', which is a rendering error for 2^31.
events.revisions: v1 9 May 2016 (only version listed on arXiv); journal version Math. Comp. 2017 per search listing.
events.delivers: Finite verification: for all 105,097,564 odd primes below 2^31, p does not divide h⁺(p). Finitely many instances of the universal claim; by the problem's own statement it moves nothing for primes above the bound.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published 2017 per a search listing; the referee process was not seen

events.directly_checkable: Computation: irregular indices and invariants recomputable per prime; the method is an adaptation of Rader's algorithm for discrete Fourier transforms (abstract). Not hand-checkable.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture at every prime below 2^31; no counterexample in that range.

ai.disclosed_cost: About 8.6 million core-hours per the search summary of the paper's text (not read in full).

events.what_happened: Sumida-Takahashi, 'A Generalized Problem Associated to the Kummer–Vandiver Conjecture', Arnold Mathematical Journal (Springer), online November 2022 per a search listing; DOI 10.1007/s40598-022-00220-3 (from the PDF's link annotation). Per search summaries of the paper (not opened: the PDF was unreadable and the Springer page redirected), it computes Iwasawa invariants of Q(√d, ζ_p) for |d| < 200 and 200 < p < 10⁶, and reports rare exceptional cases for |d| < 10 with p > 10⁶.
events.delivers: Computational data for a generalisation over Q(√d, ζ_p) with d ≠ 1. The classical statement is the case d = 1 (Q(ζ_p)). Per the search summaries it does not report a counterexample to the classical statement.
events.remains: The classical statement for all primes p (d = 1).

checked_by.what_they_did: Published online per a search listing; the referee process was not seen

events.directly_checkable: Computation over the fields Q(√d, ζ_p); not checked by hand.
events.direction: Analogue (d ≠ 1); cuts toward the generalised problem's data rather than the classical statement. Not read in full, so the direction is per search summaries only.

events.what_happened: Chakraborty and Hoque, 'On the plus parts of the class numbers of cyclotomic fields' (arXiv:2310.07501). Constructs infinite families of cyclotomic fields with nontrivial plus part: Theorems 2.3, 2.5 and 2.7 take conductor 4m with m square-free of stated shape and ℋ⁺(4m) > 1; Theorem 3.4 takes m = 3(4·3ⁿ − 1), n ≡ 0 (mod 3), and gets 3 | ℋ⁺(m). Comments field: 'To appear in Chinese Annals of Mathematics, Series B'. Published Chinese Annals of Math. Ser. B 46(2): 261–270 (2025), DOI 10.1007/s11401-025-0014-3, per a search listing (journal page not opened).
events.revisions: v1 only listed on arXiv (11 Oct 2023); journal version 2025.
events.delivers: Nontrivial plus parts for composite-conductor cyclotomic fields only (conductor 4m, or m divisible by 3). Makes no claim about a prime conductor p, so it does not bear on the problem as stated, which concerns prime p.
events.remains: The whole problem; the families are outside its scope because their conductors are not prime.

checked_by.who: Chinese Annals of Mathematics, Series B (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published 2025 per a search listing; the referee process was not seen

events.time_since_posted: about 3 years; no citing work or critique found
events.directly_checkable: Explicit families of fields (square-free m of the stated shapes); the authors' numerical examples use PARI 2.9.1 (ar5iv text).
events.direction: Does not cut against the problem: the families have composite conductor, and the problem's universal claim is over prime p only.
events.object: Explicit cyclotomic fields Q(ζ_m) with composite m (m = 4m' or m = 3(4·3ⁿ − 1), per the theorem statements in §2–3) whose plus-part class number is > 1 or divisible by 3. Explicit, not existence-based.

events.what_happened: Qin Hourong (Hou Rong Qin, Nanjing University), 'The Vandiver Conjecture and a New Conjecture on the Distribution of Irregular Primes', Acta Mathematica Sinica (Chinese Series) 67(2) (2024), 341–346, DOI 10.12386/A20230028. English abstract, via a bibliographic mirror (search.napstic.cn): 'We show that A0=A2=…=A32=0, where A is the p-Sylow subgroup of the ideal class group of Q(ζ_p).' The Chinese abstract on the journal page reads A2=A4=…=A32=0. The paper also proposes a new conjecture on the distribution of irregular primes, supported by numerical checks. Journal page: received 6 Mar 2023, revised 17 Aug 2023, published 15 Mar 2024 (issue date 7 Mar 2024). The journal page's English abstract and keywords are template placeholders.
events.delivers: States vanishing of the even components A_0 (English abstract only), A_2, …, A_32 of the p-part of the class group of Q(ζ_p). The abstract does not say for which odd primes p this holds. If it holds for every odd prime, it is a statement about 16 fixed eigenspace indices for all p, which is a restricted case of the problem's 'every even component' claim.
events.remains: Every even component of index 34 and above, for every prime; A_34 is covered for all odd p by Guo–Tao (2026, below). The full conjecture is not addressed.

checked_by.who: Acta Mathematica Sinica (Chinese Series), editorial peer review
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record; the referees are not named on the page
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication: received 6 Mar 2023, revised 17 Aug 2023, published 15 Mar 2024

events.time_since_posted: 2 years 7 months; no critique or citing work found in searches (the reference lists of later papers were not checked for it)
events.doubts: (a) The English abstract includes A_0 among the vanishing components, while the Chinese abstract starts at A_2. (b) The scope over primes is not stated in any abstract I could read, and the paper body was not readable, so whether the result holds for every odd prime or only some is unresolved.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture (vanishing); restricted to fixed small eigenspace indices.

events.what_happened: Best, Birkbeck, Brasca, Rodriguez Boidi, van de Velde and Yang, 'A complete formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem for regular primes in Lean' (arXiv:2410.01466). Lean 4/Mathlib formalization of the regular-prime case of FLT, including a formal proof of Kummer's lemma via Hilbert's Theorems 90–94. The abstract does not mention Kummer–Vandiver. Annals of Formalized Mathematics (2025) per a search listing.
events.delivers: Formal proof of FLT for regular primes. Regularity implies Kummer–Vandiver at that prime, a standard fact the formalization does not extend. Covers regular primes only; says nothing about irregular primes.
events.remains: Every irregular prime, and so the universal claim.
events.time_since_posted: 2 years; the paper's Kummer–Vandiver relevance is not discussed in the abstract
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on regular primes; not a new result about the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Mihăilescu, talk 'The simplicity of the class group of the p-cyclotomic field', Westlake University, 15 Nov 2024 (its.westlake.edu.cn abstract). Abstract: 'Then we derive three consequences from the truth of the Kummer-Vandiver Conjecture', including the structure of the p-primary part of the class group of the maximal subreal field. No write-up found, so the talk date is used.
events.delivers: Three consequences conditional on the conjecture being true. No unconditional result.
events.direction: None: the consequences are derived from the conjecture, so they do not bear on its truth.

events.what_happened: Chen, Cummins, Eltschig, Grubisic, Haller, Hong, Kurghinyan, Lau, Leather, Lee, Markosyan, Ono, Patel, Pendharkar, Rathi, Schneidman, Seeker, Sengupta, Sinha, Xin and Zhang, 'Almost all primes are partially regular' (arXiv:2602.05090; authors listed alphabetically). Theorem 1.1: for fixed α > 1/2 and M_α(p) = ⌊√p/(log p)^α⌋, the number of primes p ≤ X that are not M_α(p)-regular is at most C_α·X/(log X)^{2α}. Corollary 1.4: for almost every prime, A_p(ω^{2k}) = 0 for 2 ≤ 2k ≤ M_α(p), which the paper calls a 'partial Vandiver' result, and says considers 'a weaker form of Vandiver's Conjecture, which pertains to the triviality of initial ranges of the eigenspaces'. The paper states the full conjecture is not proved. Axiom Math blog post by its CEO, 5 Feb 2026, announces the result and says the theorem was 'autonomously proved and formalized in Lean by AxiomProver'. Lean repository: github.com/AxiomMath/partial-regularity (MIT licence).
events.revisions: v1 only: submitted Wed 4 Feb 2026 22:20:52 UTC; no later version listed on the arXiv page read on 12 Oct 2026. The blog's Theorem 1.3 and the paper's Theorem 1.1 are the same statement under different numbering.
events.delivers: For each α > 1/2, all but a density-zero set of primes satisfy A_p(ω^{2k}) = 0 for every even 2 ≤ 2k ≤ M_α(p) ≈ √p/(log p)^α. The result covers an initial range of even eigenspace indices for almost all primes. It does not establish p ∤ h⁺(p) for any specific prime, because h⁺ involves all even eigenspaces up to p−3. Lean remark 1.2 (extension file) gives C_α = 10 for all α > 1/2.
events.remains: (i) For the density-zero set of exceptional primes, nothing. (ii) For every prime p, the even eigenspaces with 2k > M_α(p) up to p−3, which is the part p ∤ h⁺ requires. (iii) The full conjecture, which the authors say is not proved.

checked_by.who: Ken Ribet, Ashvin Swaminathan, Ila Varma
checked_by.qualification: Ribet is a leading specialist in the Herbrand–Ribet theorem, which the paper cites as [15]; the qualifications of Swaminathan and Varma were not checked
checked_by.what_they_did: Acknowledged in the paper for comments on an earlier version. No statement of agreement, endorsement or verification was found.

events.time_since_posted: 8 months; no referee report, review or public verification found. A later paper (Guo–Tao, Sep 2026) cites and uses the result, which is use, not verification.

machine_checked.system: Lean 4 with Mathlib (the paper's §4.2 states Lean 4.26.0; the repository README states Lean 4.34.0-rc2 and says compatibility with other versions is not guaranteed)

events.directly_checkable: The statement of Theorem 1.1 is elementary and the Lean files (problem.lean, solution.lean) are said to be the formal statement and proof. The Lean sources were not read, so the fidelity of problem.lean to problem.tex is unchecked.
events.doubts: (1) Authorship and conflict of interest: the paper calls itself 'a case study and test case for AxiomProver, an AI tool currently under development' (Remark 1.9). The author list is the team building the system (search summaries also place the authors at Axiom Math; the arXiv page read did not show affiliations). This is a signal about who produced the result, not a mathematical objection. (2) Version mismatch: the paper states Lean 4.26.0 (§4.2), while the repository README states Lean 4.34.0-rc2 and says other versions are not guaranteed to compile the same way. (3) The natural-language input (problem.tex) and the Lean statement (problem.lean) were not compared, and the paper does not say who wrote problem.tex. (4) Reflection and Herbrand–Ribet are cited, not re-proved; their inputs are external. (5) The paper does not state whether the derivation of Corollary 1.4 from Theorem 1.1 (via Leopoldt's reflection principle) is formalized. (6) A search summary says the paper is not being submitted to a journal; the arXiv page shows no journal reference, and I did not verify the summary.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: shows the initial even eigenspaces vanish for almost all primes. It does not assert that the conjecture fails or holds at any particular prime.

systems.name: AxiomProver
systems.what_it_did: Per the authors, given only a natural-language statement of the density theorem (Theorem 1.1 in the paper; Theorem 1.3 in the blog), it autonomously produced a Lean 4/Mathlib formal statement and a complete Lean-verified proof. The Axiom blog says the human side 'asked it to construct the analytic proof that links these concepts to the distribution of primes'. The cited external theorems (Ribet, Leopoldt, Herbrand–Ribet) were not reproved by the system. The paper calls the system 'an AI tool currently under development'. No underlying model is named in the sources read.
systems.basis_quote: No human assistance was provided. ... After AxiomProver generated a solution, the human authors wrote this paper (without the use of AI) for human readers.

events.what_happened: Nada, Sasaki and Sumida-Takahashi, 'Iwasawa invariants and exceptional pairs of certain abelian fields' (arXiv:2608.05517). Studies Q(√d, ζ_p) with d ≠ 1; computes Iwasawa invariants and 'exceptional pairs' (p, χω_p^k) by computing arithmetic elements modulo primes; reports 15 new exceptional pairs for |d| < 200 (or |d| < 10 with p < 30,000,000 per the abstract as summarised), and one example with λ = 2. The paper says its data were obtained 'by seven personal computers with 76 cores (152 threads) for about five years'. No AI system is named.
events.delivers: Iwasawa-invariant and exceptional-pair data for the generalised problem over Q(√d, ζ_p), d ≠ 1. It does not treat d = 1, the classical statement.
events.remains: The classical statement for all primes.
events.direction: Analogue (d ≠ 1). The abstract does not say whether 'exceptional pair' is an exception to the generalised statement; it does not bear on d = 1.

events.what_happened: Guo and Tao, 'Density of Vanishing of Certain Eigenspaces of Cyclotomic Class Groups' (arXiv:2609.13932; Nanjing University and Hefei University of Technology). (i) For even d ≥ 4, on a relative density-one set of primes p ≡ d+1 (mod 2d), the odd block of eigenspaces has order at most p^{φ(d)/2−1}. For d ∈ {4, 6} both blocks vanish on that set (Corollary 1.2); for d ∈ {8, 10, 12} the odd block has order at most p. (ii) Theorem 1.3: 'For every odd prime p, A_34 = 0'. Appendix A: reflection and Herbrand's theorem reduce this to one prime p₀ = 151628697551, checked by a cyclotomic-unit test in PARI/GP that the appendix reports returned PASS after about three hours. The paper cites Chen et al. [5] (arXiv:2602.05090) and states that Chen et al. 'proved that, for each α>1/2, a density-one set of primes satisfies A_{p−2k} = A_{2k} = 0 for 2 ≤ 2k ≤ √p/(log p)^α'.
events.revisions: v1 only listed (submitted Sat 12 Sep 2026 13:25:58 UTC).
events.delivers: (i) Vanishing of specified eigenspace blocks for a relative density-one set of primes within the congruence classes p ≡ d+1 (mod 2d), d ∈ {4, 6}. (ii) Vanishing of the single eigenspace A_34 for every odd prime p, via a finite computation. Neither covers all even eigenspaces for all primes.
events.remains: For d ∈ {8, 10, 12} only a bound on the odd block; the even eigenspaces for other indices and for primes outside those classes; the full conjecture.
events.directly_checkable: Theorem 1.3 reduces to one prime p₀ = 151628697551 and a PARI/GP computation described in Appendix A; reproducible in principle. The program was not inspected.
events.direction: Consistent with vanishing: partial results toward the conjecture, with no claim against it.

disputes.summary: An investor tear sheet on Axiom Math ('AS OF AUG 2026', 'compiled from public disclosures and press', no source given for the item) says AxiomProver 'verifiably proved the Partial Vandiver Conjecture' and dates it in its timeline to 'Nov–Dec 2025'. The arXiv preprint's first version is 4 Feb 2026, and the Axiom blog post is dated 5 Feb 2026. I found no earlier dated written argument. The event is dated to arXiv v1 under the date rule. If a November–December 2025 public written argument exists, the date of the Chen et al. event moves.

summary: Found: no resolution of the classical statement since 26 January 2024, and one new partial result that is machine-generated. Chen et al. (arXiv:2602.05090, 4 Feb 2026; 21 authors, Axiom Math) prove that for almost all primes the even eigenspaces A_p(ω^{2k}) vanish for 2 ≤ 2k ≤ √p/(log p)^α (α > 1/2). The paper calls this a partial Vandiver result, states that the full conjecture is not proved, and does not give p ∤ h⁺ for any specific prime. The authors say AxiomProver generated the proof of the density theorem from a natural-language statement, formalized it in Lean/Mathlib, and that the human authors then wrote the paper 'without the use of AI'. I read those sentences in the arXiv HTML; I did not run the Lean code, did not read the Lean sources, and did not confirm that the Corollary's reflection step is formalized. The paper's Lean version (4.26.0) differs from the repository README (4.34.0-rc2). Close call: whether this is progress on the problem or a restricted analogue. It moves the conjecture's own quantity for almost all primes, but only for an initial range of indices and density-one primes; both readings are recorded. Guo–Tao (arXiv:2609.13932, Sep 2026; no AI system named) prove A_34 = 0 for every odd prime through a finite PARI/GP check reduced to one prime, and density-one vanishing in residue classes for d ∈ {4, 6}; they cite Chen et al. and use it. Qin (Acta Math. Sinica 2024) claims A_0 = A_2 = … = A_32 = 0. The English abstract includes A_0, the Chinese abstract starts at A_2, and the scope over primes is not stated in any abstract I could read. If it holds for all odd primes, it is a fixed-index result, not a resolution. Stolin (arXiv:2001.09702, first posted 27 Jan 2020, last revised 15 Jun 2020) claims a full proof for all odd primes. It predates the window and has no journal publication, published review, refutation or citing work that I could find. The v4 main text says the author replaced the proof of Theorem 3.6 after questions, and several steps are sketched or cited without proof (§1.1, §1.4, §3). I treat it as an unverified claimed proof and record the reasons on both sides. Finite verifications (Buhler–Harvey to 163,577,356; Hart–Harvey–Ong to 2^31, Math. Comp. 2017) move nothing under §2.1. Other events are analogues or conditional: Chakraborty–Hoque (2023/2025) use only composite conductors; Nada–Sasaki–Sumida-Takahashi (Aug 2026) treat d ≠ 1; Sumida-Takahashi (2022) is a generalised problem, read only through search summaries because the PDF was unreadable; Mihăilescu's 2010 preprint and his Nov 2024 talk are conditional; Best et al. (Oct 2024) formalize FLT for regular primes in Lean, which says nothing about irregular primes. The Wikipedia article (fetched; last edited 19 July 2026) still lists the problem as open. Its status text dates from 2011 and it mentions none of the 2024–2026 items. AI search: the only system credited with mathematics in any event is AxiomProver. Searches linking OpenAI, Google DeepMind or Anthropic models to this problem found nothing. The Stolin proof, the Qin scope and the Axiom Lean check are the three items that could change the picture most, and each is recorded with the evidence in hand.
competing_reading: The Chen et al. result could be read as a substantive advance on the problem, not only an analogue: it is a theorem about the conjecture's own quantity (the even eigenspaces of the p-part of the class group of Q(ζ_p)), it is the first result in the window to move that quantity for almost all primes, and it was formalized in Lean. On this reading it counts as partial progress by AI. The opposing reading: its restriction to density-one primes and to an initial index range of size about √p/(log p)^α leaves the claim for any individual prime, and for the full even part, untouched; the authors say so themselves. Stolin's 2020 proof, if correct, is a full resolution and would supersede every other event; the reading against it is that a claimed proof of a famous conjecture has had no publication or review for six years, and the v4 text itself reports a replaced step. Qin's A_0–A_32 result is a restricted-index statement if it holds for all primes, but if it holds only for some primes it is a finite-case statement and moves nothing.
what_would_settle_it: For Chen et al.: the Lean sources (problem.lean against problem.tex, the sorry status of solution.lean, and whether Corollary 1.4 is formalized) under the Lean version the authors used, plus journal refereeing. For Stolin: a referee report or a published refutation or acceptance of the replaced Theorem 3.6 argument and of the sketched extension to all primes. For Qin: the full theorem statement in the journal text, specifically whether A_0 through A_32 vanish for every odd prime p or only for some. For the date question: any written argument on the Partial Vandiver result dated before 4 Feb 2026.
